questions.q: A static margin of SM = 10 % MAC means that when C_L rises by 0.1, the pitching moment about the CG changes by…
options: +0.01 (nose-up)
−0.01 (nose-down)
−0.10 (nose-down)
0, the moment does not change
questions.explain: dCm/dCL = −SM, so ΔCm = −0.1·0.1 = −0.01. The nose-down moment brings the airplane back to its original angle of attack.

questions.q: A swept wing: root chord 300 mm, tip chord 180 mm, leading-edge sweep 25°. The pilot put the CG at 75 mm (a quarter of the root chord). What happens?
options: A normal CG, margin about 8 %
Tail heavy: the CG is behind the NP, the wing is unstable
Nose heavy: the NP is at 168 mm, margin about 38 % MAC
Neutral CG: the CG coincides with the NP, margin about zero
questions.explain: The aerodynamic center of a swept wing lies at a quarter of the MAC, and the MAC leading edge is 107 mm aft. NP = 107 + 0.25·245 = 168 mm, margin (168 − 75)/245 ≈ 38 %.

questions.q: How does the tail volume coefficient V_h = S_h·l_h/(S·MAC) affect the neutral point position?
options: Larger V_h: the NP moves aft, the CG can go further aft
Larger V_h: the NP moves forward, the CG must move forward
V_h affects only directional stability, not the NP
The NP is always at 25 % MAC; V_h changes only the trim deflection
questions.explain: h_n = h_ac + η·V_h·(a_t/a_w)·(1 − dε/dα): the larger the tail or the longer the arm, the further aft the NP. That is why on an airplane with a tail the CG can be at 40 % MAC or more.

questions.q: Why does a flying wing need a reflex airfoil or raised elevons?
options: To lower the stall speed with more camber
To get Cm0 > 0: without it there is no trim at SM > 0
To move the neutral point aft and increase the margin
To reduce the induced drag in cruise
questions.explain: Cm = Cm0 − SM·C_L, level flight at C_L,trim = Cm0/SM. With a positive margin you need a positive Cm0, and an ordinary cambered airfoil gives Cm0 < 0.

questions.q: The polar C_D = C_D0 + k·C_L². At what C_L is the maximum L/D reached?
options: C_L = C_Lmax / 1.3
C_L = C_D0/k
questions.explain: C_D/C_L is minimal when the induced part equals the parasite part: k·C_L² = C_D0. √(3·C_D0/k) is minimum power (endurance).

questions.q: An electric airplane: V_md = 10.8 m/s, V_mp = 8.2 m/s, V_s = 9.4 m/s. Which speed do you take for maximum endurance?
options: 8.2 m/s: minimum power, which is what endurance is
About 1.2–1.3·V_s (11–12 m/s): V_mp is below the stall
10.8 m/s: the maximum L/D also gives endurance
As high as possible: the battery delivers more energy at higher current
questions.explain: V_mp lies below V_s, and you cannot fly there. Endurance is limited by the safe minimum speed (`AIRSPEED_MIN`), not by the polar.

questions.q: An ArduPlane log fragment, steady cruise in FBWA. What is most likely?
options: Tail heavy: the airplane constantly needs down elevator to stay level
Nose heavy or wrong trim: the integrator holds up elevator
Pitch oscillation from too large a P
Airspeed sensor failure
questions.explain: Per the ArduPlane documentation, a persistently positive PIDP.I means up elevator is needed: a heavy nose or an incorrect trim. The error is small and the pitch is tracked, so there is no oscillation.

questions.q: Glide test: mass 2.7 kg, S = 0.41 m², AR 8.2, e = 0.8, L/D = 10.5 measured at 12 m/s. What does this measurement give you?
options: The neutral point position without computing V_h
The stall speed through C_Lmax = C_L/L·D
C_D0 ≈ 0.044: C_D = C_L/(L/D), minus the induced part
The Oswald factor e, if you assume C_D0 is zero
questions.explain: C_L = 2mg/(ρV²S) ≈ 0.73, C_D = 0.73/10.5 ≈ 0.070, k·C_L² ≈ 0.026, hence C_D0 ≈ 0.044. With it the polar is recomputed from real data.
